name: Jim Chanos
current_role: Founder, Chanos & Company (formerly Kynikos Associates); closed outside-capital hedge funds end-2023, now advisory/commentary
profile: Greek-American short seller who founded Kynikos Associates in 1985 with $16M and became famous for shorting Enron before its 2001 collapse. He returned outside capital at end-2023 and now runs Chanos & Company in an advisory capacity while remaining a prominent market commentator, notably sceptical of AI/data-center accounting.
interesting_fact: He has been an outspoken critic of AI infrastructure economics, arguing on X that GPU depreciation lives at hyperscalers are too long and calling neoclouds like CoreWeave 'financial conduits, not technology companies' - directly relevant to a data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in a Greek immigrant family that ran a chain of dry-cleaning shops in Milwaukee; his first big call came at Gilford Securities in 1982, when a cash-flow analysis led him to a sell recommendation on Baldwin-United, which went bankrupt in 1983. 'Kynikos' is Greek for 'cynic'.
notes: Very media-friendly and appears on many podcasts; his AI capex/depreciation skepticism makes him a strong contrarian guest. X is the most active public channel. Avoid the 2024 Conlon Holdings dispute.

name: Vivek Chand Burman
current_role: Patriarch of the V.C. Burman branch of the Dabur promoter family; former chairman of Dabur India (1998-2007)
profile: The oldest member of the Burman clan behind Dabur, the Ayurvedic consumer-goods company his great-grandfather S.K. Burman founded in Kolkata in 1884. He joined Dabur in 1954, chaired it from 1998 for about a decade, then handed over to nephew Anand Burman; his son Mohit became Dabur chairman in 2022. The family also holds a stake in battery maker Eveready Industries.
interesting_fact: Dabur began as a physician's home dispensary of Ayurvedic medicines in 1884; 360 ONE ranks the 'VC Burman and Family' #39 among India's wealthiest families (about $5.5bn) on Dabur shares, with brands like Dabur Chyawanprash, Honey and Amla Hair Oil leading their categories.
notes: Very elderly and low-profile (joined Dabur in 1954); alive status inferred from current Forbes listing, no death reports found. Realistic route is via Dabur corporate communications or son Mohit Burman's offices. Weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast except via the Eveready (batteries) stake.

name: Jess Jackson
current_role: Deceased (founder of Kendall-Jackson / Jackson Family Wines)
profile: Jess Stonestreet Jackson Jr. (1930-2011), founder of Kendall-Jackson and Jackson Family Wines, died on April 21, 2011 at age 81 at his home in Geyserville, California.
notes: Died April 21, 2011 (source: https://prnewswire.com/news-releases/wine-icon-jess-stonestreet-jackson-passes-away-120361079.html). The business is now run as Jackson Family Wines by his family; profile skipped per instructions.

name: Casey Foyt
current_role: Owner & Executive Vice President, Indianapolis Colts (since June 2025)
profile: Middle daughter of the late Jim Irsay and granddaughter of Robert Irsay, who bought the Colts in 1972. She and sisters Carlie Irsay-Gordon and Kalen Jackson inherited equal ~33.3% stakes in the franchise after their father's death in May 2025; she became Owner & EVP after 13 seasons as vice chair/owner, focusing on marketing and community relations.
interesting_fact: Before joining the Colts in 2007, she worked for the NFL in London planning the league's first regular-season game outside North America - Giants vs. Dolphins at Wembley in October 2007.
deep_cut_fact: An Indiana University sports-marketing graduate, she helped revitalize the Indianapolis Colts Women's Organization and planned the group's first major fundraiser in 2007; as a high-schooler she answered phones at the Colts' front desk.
notes: Low public profile compared with sister Carlie (CEO). Best route is the Colts' communications/front office. Family is active in mental-health campaign Kicking the Stigma (led by sister Kalen). Little energy/data-center angle.

name: Arthur Demoulas
current_role: Major shareholder and former president & CEO (2008-2025) of DeMoulas Super Markets (Market Basket); no longer in management
profile: Arthur T. Demoulas (b. 1955), grandson of the Greek immigrants who opened DeMoulas Market in Lowell, Mass., in 1917, ran New England grocer Market Basket as CEO from 2008, growing sales from about $3bn to $4bn and staff from 14,000 to 25,000. He and his sisters control the company; the board removed him from management in 2025.
interesting_fact: In 2014, after the board fired him, Market Basket employees and customers staged weeks of walkouts and boycotts until he was reinstated and his side of the family bought out their cousins - a rare case of rank-and-file workers successfully campaigning for a CEO's return.
deep_cut_fact: In 1989, after the family board rejected his proposal to start a pharmacy division, he founded his own drugstore chain, Lee Drug, and sold its nine stores to Walgreens in 1990. In high school in Andover he played running back on the football team.
notes: Sensitive timing: suspended May 2025, fired Sept 2025; a Delaware court upheld the removal in April 2026 and he said he would not appeal - avoid this topic. Market Basket's corporate channels represent the board, not him; no personal/public channel found. Very private and press-averse. Web search budget ran out during this person.

name: Alessandro Rosano
current_role: Founder of HeyDude (sold to Crocs in 2022); Hong Kong-based entrepreneur
profile: Italian entrepreneur from Pistoia, near Florence, who founded comfort-shoe brand HeyDude and, with partner/U.S. distributor Daniele Guidi, sold it to Crocs for $2.5bn in 2022. HeyDude sales rose from $20M in 2018 to $581M in 2021, and the brand later passed $1bn in annual revenue under Crocs. He runs his businesses from Hong Kong.
interesting_fact: Rosano built HeyDude with no outside investment and minimal marketing before selling it to Crocs for $2.5 billion.
deep_cut_fact: Before HeyDude he launched several brands, including WeWood, a wooden wristwatch line, and Baldo, wooden clogs with springs built into the heels.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal website or verified social accounts found. HeyDude press now runs through Crocs and would not represent him. Web search budget ran out before this person, so current ventures are unverified.

name: Liu Jingkang
profile: Liu Jingkang (J.K. Liu, ~35) founded 360-degree and action-camera maker Insta360 in Shenzhen in 2015 with classmates from Nanjing University's computer-science program. Backed by Qiming, IDG and Suning, it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in June 2025 and now rivals DJI and GoPro, holding roughly 73% of the global 360-degree camera market.
interesting_fact: NASA used Insta360 Pro cameras to live-stream the InSight Mars landing from mission control in 2018 (a project that won an Emmy) and again for the Perseverance landing in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: His first product was not a camera but a smartphone live-streaming app; the idea for 360-degree video came from wanting to record and share the feeling of being at a music concert, which led to a phone accessory that turned a smartphone into a 360 camera.
notes: Young, product-focused founder; good entrepreneurship story but little energy/data-center angle. Insta360 has offices in Los Angeles, Tokyo and Berlin; route via company PR (press contact not machine-readable on the JS site). Web search budget was exhausted, so no personal social accounts verified.

name: James Richardson
current_role: Family listing tied to James Richardson & Sons, Limited (Winnipeg); current leaders are CEO Hartley T. Richardson, President Thor R. Richardson and Chair Daniel R. Hursh
profile: The listing appears to represent the Richardson family behind James Richardson & Sons, Limited (JRSL), a private Winnipeg conglomerate founded in 1857 as a one-man grain merchant in Kingston, Ontario. Now in its sixth generation, JRSL spans grain and food processing (Richardson International), oil (Tundra Oil & Gas), pipelines (Kingston Midstream), insurance, trucking and real estate.
interesting_fact: JRSL's Tundra Oil & Gas is Manitoba's largest oil producer (~30,000 bbl/day of light crude, ~3,500 wells), and Kingston Midstream runs about 2,300 km of crude gathering pipelines - a strong energy angle for the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: The company's founding motto, still quoted on its leadership page, is from James Richardson in 1857: 'Our goal is to be the kind of business organization in which people can place their trust.'
notes: No living 'James Richardson' appears in JRSL leadership; the namesake founder died in the 19th century and the Hon. James A. Richardson chaired 1966-68. Treat as a family entry; the most relevant podcast guest would be CEO Hartley T. Richardson or President Thor R. Richardson. No Forbes profile URL was provided.

name: Frank McCourt
current_role: Executive Chairman, McCourt Global; founder & Executive Chairman, Project Liberty
profile: Boston-born real-estate developer from a five-generation construction family who bought the LA Dodgers in 2004 for $430M and sold them in 2012 for $2.2B. He reinvested via McCourt Global (real estate, sports incl. Olympique de Marseille, tech, media) and in 2023 stepped back as CEO to focus on Project Liberty, his $500M push for a decentralized, user-controlled internet.
interesting_fact: He led 'The People's Bid' consortium to buy TikTok's US business and in 2026 launched the Premier Jumping League, a global show-jumping circuit backed by a guaranteed $300M prize pot; his book 'Our Biggest Fight' came out in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: In 1977 he left his father's road-contracting company to found The McCourt Company; its first and best-known project was the Union Wharf Condominium on Boston Harbor, and he later assembled 24 acres that helped shape today's South Boston Seaport District.
notes: Very accessible on internet-governance/tech topics; Project Liberty's DSNP protocol and AI/data-ownership agenda are a natural podcast hook. Avoid the Dodgers bankruptcy and divorce. Best route: press@mccourt.com or Project Liberty.

name: Family Peugeot
current_role: Family group controlling Établissements Peugeot Frères and listed holding company Peugeot Invest (a leading shareholder of Stellantis)
profile: The Peugeot family of Franche-Comté has been in industry since 1810, when it started a steel foundry; Automobiles Peugeot followed in 1896. The family invests through Établissements Peugeot Frères and Peugeot Invest (founded 1929 as FFP), which holds a Stellantis stake via Peugeot 1810 and, since Robert Peugeot's diversification push from 2002-03, minority stakes, private equity and real estate.
interesting_fact: Before cars, the family made saws, coffee grinders (1840), steel corset blades and crinoline hoops, then bicycles; its 1874 'Z' table pepper mill is still in production via the family-owned Peugeot Saveurs.
deep_cut_fact: The Peugeot lion logo, trademarked by Émile Peugeot on 20 November 1858, originally symbolized the speed, strength and flexibility of the family's steel saw blades - not cars.
notes: This is a family entry, not an individual; for a guest, the natural spokesperson is the chair of Peugeot Invest / Établissements Peugeot Frères (Robert Peugeot historically led it). Current chair not verified because web search budget was exhausted. Route via Image 7 (PR agency).

name: Hans Thomann
current_role: Managing Director (Geschäftsführer) and sole owner, Thomann GmbH (Musikhaus Thomann), Burgebrach/Treppendorf, Germany
profile: Hans (Johann) Thomann Jr. (b. 1962) took over the music shop his father, a travelling musician, founded in the Bavarian village of Treppendorf in 1954, running it from 1990. He turned it into the world's largest music-gear retailer by revenue (about EUR1.1bn in 2020) through mail-order catalogues and early e-commerce, with 1,800+ staff from 55 countries, still headquartered in Treppendorf.
interesting_fact: Thomann was the first German music retailer to sell online, in 1996; incoming e-mails were printed out, carried to departments and answered by post, and the web shop still did DM 800,000 in its first year.
deep_cut_fact: His father gave up life as a travelling musician in 1954 to open the shop and studied trumpet in Würzburg on the side; by 1989 the family firm had also built 24 recording studios in southern Germany, including for broadcasters. Hans Jr. started in the business at age 12.
notes: hans@thomann.de is published in Thomann's legal imprint (Impressum) as the managing director's address - a legitimate but high-volume channel; marketing@thomann.de also appears on company pages. Very press-shy; rarely gives interviews. Strong e-commerce/logistics story.

name: Michael Cagney
current_role: Co-founder & Executive Chairman, Figure Technology Solutions (Nasdaq: FIGR)
profile: Fintech serial founder: Wells Fargo trader, then founder of wealth-software firm Finaplex and macro hedge fund Cabezon, then co-founder/CEO of SoFi (2011-2017). In 2018 he co-founded Figure with June Ou to originate, trade and finance loans on blockchain rails (Provenance Blockchain); Figure listed on Nasdaq in September 2025, where he serves as executive chairman.
interesting_fact: Figure was the first company to put consumer loans on a blockchain, and its Provenance chain was in 2025 the largest public blockchain by real-world assets; Figure Markets also issued $YLDS, the first SEC-registered yield-bearing stablecoin security.
deep_cut_fact: SoFi began as a Stanford GSB class project during his 2010 Sloan Fellowship: a pilot seeded with $2M from 40 Stanford alumni, lent to 100 business students. He studied applied economics at UC Santa Cruz.
notes: Outspoken on stablecoins, the GENIUS Act and DeFi; he writes publicly and is active on X (handle not verified here because the web search budget ran out). Avoid the 2017 SoFi departure. Route via press@figure.com.

name: Purnendu Chatterjee
current_role: Founder & Chairman, The Chatterjee Group (TCG), New York
profile: IIT Kharagpur and UC Berkeley (PhD, operations research) engineer who was a McKinsey partner, then founded TCG and for over 13 years advised Soros's Quantum funds, overseeing $3bn+ of investments. TCG's holdings include Lummus Technology, Haldia Petrochemicals, MCPI, LabVantage and TCG Digital, plus the TCG CREST research institutes.
interesting_fact: His group owns Lummus Technology, a major licensor of refining, petrochemical and energy-transition process technology, and Haldia Petrochemicals in West Bengal; TCG CREST includes a Research Institute for Sustainable Energy (RISE) - strong energy angle.
deep_cut_fact: His philosophy is 'wealth to knowledge': profits fund TCG CREST research centres in quantum engineering (CQuERE), neuroscience (CHINTA) and AI, and TCG is building an AI 'Infrastructure for Intelligence' (i4i) as a shared knowledge layer for translational science. He began as a research associate at Stanford Research Institute (1974-76).
notes: Excellent fit (petrochemicals, energy-transition tech via Lummus, AI infrastructure via i4i). The contact page lists a placeholder email (hello@websitename.com) - use the web form or TCG's NY office line instead. Lummus Technology's own media team is another route.

name: Peng Hao
profile: Peng Hao (~59) founded Shenzhen Sunway Communication, a maker of RF components such as antenna and wireless-charging modules, high-speed connectors/cables and MLCCs, which listed in Shenzhen in 2010. Sunway now has 10,000+ employees and 2025 revenue of about CNY 8.9bn, supplying smartphone OEMs and expanding into AI servers, data centers, satellites and vehicles.
interesting_fact: Sunway lists AI servers and data centers among its target markets (high-frequency, high-speed connectors and cables), and it acquired antenna maker Laird Technologies (Beijing) in 2012 to win global smartphone customers.
deep_cut_fact: He started Sunway in his dormitory in Shajin Changxing Industrial Park in Shenzhen; the company commits at least 8% of revenue to R&D each year and had filed 5,498 patent applications by end-2025.
notes: Low international profile; likely needs Mandarin outreach via the company's marketing or securities/IR office. Relevant data-center hardware angle (high-speed interconnects). The dorm-founding detail is from Forbes; the R&D/patent figures are from the company site.
